stem: Ben can paint a wall in 6 days. Carlo can paint the same wall in 12 days. They work together for 2 days, then Ben leaves. How many more days will Carlo need to finish the wall?
hints: Split the job into two parts: the work done together, then the work Carlo does alone.
Together they paint 1/6 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 of the wall per day. How much is done in 2 days?
Find the part left (1 − the part done). Carlo paints 1/12 of the wall per day, so divide the part left by 1/12.

solution.methodName: Work rates: rate = 1 ÷ time, then add the rates

steps.action: Let x = the extra days Carlo works alone.
Rates: Ben paints 1/6 of the wall per day, and Carlo paints 1/12 per day.
Together: 1/6 + 1/12 = 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 of the wall per day.
In 2 days together: 2 × 1/4 = 2/4 = 1/2 of the wall.

steps.why: Dividing by 1/12 is the same as multiplying by 12.

steps.action: Check: in 6 days Carlo paints 6 × 1/12 = 1/2 of the wall. 1/2 + 1/2 = 1 whole wall. Carlo needs 6 more days.

trapNotes.2: This is the time left if both kept working (4 − 2 days). Ben leaves, so only Carlo's rate counts.
trapNotes.10: This is 12 − 2. It takes away the 2 days but ignores the work Ben did during those days.
trapNotes.12: This is Carlo's time for the whole wall. Half the wall is already painted after the 2 days together.
